correctness.rationale: Eq. (3.1) factors exactly as \(R_0(v)=(\mu R_S+vR_V)/(\mu+v)\). The derivative, limiting endpoint, threshold condition, and corrected \((v, eta_1)\) boundary follow by elementary algebra. For the Figure 1 values, the \((E,A)\) Jacobian block has determinant proportional to \(1-R_0\); the recomputed \(R_0pprox3.66948\) therefore implies a positive eigenvalue, explicitly \(\lambda_+pprox0.180134\). The standalone verifier reproduces every numerical value from the printed decimals.

originality.rationale: The primary article states that increasing the vaccination rate suppresses transmission and reports a critical rate near \(0.023\), but it does not expose the endpoint interpolation or the breakthrough floor. Exact-title, DOI, threshold-language, and equation-pattern searches found the source and related imperfect-vaccine literature but no correction or source-specific derivation of this incompatibility. Earlier imperfect-vaccine work contains the general principle that high coverage may fail when efficacy is low; the accepted claim is narrower and source-specific.
residual_risks: An unindexed corrigendum or private author note could document different intended parameter scaling.
The published figures may have been generated with code inputs different from the printed decimals; this result intentionally makes no claim about undisclosed code.

value.rationale: The paper uses its reproduction number to make a concrete vaccination-policy claim. The exact endpoint decomposition shows when increasing vaccination can or cannot cross threshold and demonstrates that the paper's own breakthrough coefficient places its stated Table 2 scenario above threshold for every vaccination rate. This directly changes the interpretation of the reported critical rate and the disease-free numerical illustration.
